channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: 'O brasileiro adora uma pulseira VIP': como o desejo de status, além da renda, dita a satisfação do eleitor; ouça 'O Assunto'
item.description: Qualitative research in 'mirror rooms' shows that Brazilian voters, especially independents, seek not just income but a sense of social ascent and distinction. Social programs are now seen as rights, not favors, reducing gratitude-driven electoral impact. Status symbols — such as upgrading phones, flying by plane, or accessing public universities — have become key indicators of voter satisfaction, reflecting social mobility rather than mere economic improvement.

item.title: Eleição que definirá Nunes Marques como novo presidente do TSE será na semana que vem, diz Cármen
item.description: TSE President Cármen Lúcia announced that the election to appoint Nunes Marques as president and André Mendonça as vice-president will take place next Tuesday (14), advancing the vote due to the 2026 elections. The inauguration is expected in late May, before her term ends on June 3, giving the new leaders over 100 days to manage the electoral process ahead of the October 2026 general elections. Nunes Marques stated that reducing absenteeism will be a priority, maintaining partnerships with digital platforms and developing AI-detection tools with universities.

item.title: Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro veem perdas com brigas e ensaiam aproximaçăo
item.description: Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro are attempting a rapprochement after recognizing that public feuds result in mutual losses, with early signs including Michelle sharing a Flávio post on April 2 about Autism Day. The rapprochement is being supported by right-wing leaders such as Damares Alves and Valdemar Costa Neto, and encouraged by former President Jair Bolsonaro, now under house arrest, who is urging family unity. However, tensions remain with Carlos and Eduardo Bolsonaro, and Michelle’s return to politics may be delayed until the second half of the year due to family considerations.

item.title: Governo calcula que R$ 7 bilhões do FGTS podem ser liberados a 10 milhões de pessoas para pagamento de dívidas, diz ministro
item.description: Labor Minister Luiz Marinho announced that the government is evaluating the release of R$ 7 billion from the FGTS to approximately 10 million workers for debt payment. The funds are residual amounts linked to the anniversary withdrawal option and bank loans, not fully released by Caixa in 2025 despite two provisional measures signed by Lula. The initiative responds to the president’s concern over household indebtedness and aims to use FGTS as a tool for financial relief.

item.title: Câmara rejeita mudança emendas feitas pelo Senado na MP do seguro-defeso; acompanhe
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies rejected the Senate's amendments to Provisional Measure 1323/25, maintaining the version approved by deputies on Tuesday. The MP changes the rules for the closed-season fishing benefit, establishing new registration conditions to prevent fraud and authorizing payment of outstanding installments in 2026. The text now proceeds to presidential sanction, with a projected R$ 7.9 billion for the benefit in 2026, excluding arrears.

item.title: A justificativa de Mara Gabrilli para votar contra a indicação de Jorge Messias ao STF
item.description: Senator Mara Gabrilli (PSD-SP) voted against the nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, criticizing the choice as based on personal loyalty and political convenience rather than institutional strengthening. She lamented that the government missed the opportunity to nominate a woman with renowned legal expertise, accusing Lula of seeking to turn the Supreme Court into a group of allies rather than an independent and plural institution.

item.title: Novo publica manifesto contra indicação de Messias ao STF
item.description: The Novo party published a manifesto titled 'Messias not' against the nomination of Jorge Messias, the Attorney General of the Union, to the Federal Supreme Court (STF) to fill the vacancy left by Luís Roberto Barroso. The text states that Messias has a 'political and professional history incompatible with the importance of the position,' questioning his suitability for the Supreme Court. The manifesto was released on social media on Thursday, the 9th, as part of the opposition to President Lula's (PT) choice.

item.title: Alcolumbre quer pautar votação de veto de Lula ao PL da Dosimetria ‘o mais rápido possível’
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre said he is in talks with Chamber President Hugo Motta to schedule a vote on overriding President Lula’s veto of the Dosimetry Bill, which would reduce sentences for Jair Bolsonaro and others convicted in the January 8 attacks. The bill, approved by Congress in December 2023, was fully vetoed by Lula in January 2024, who framed it as a defense of democracy. Alcolumbre stressed the timing is his prerogative and that the agenda may not include all pending vetoes.

item.title: PT do Rio Grande do Sul aceita apoiar PDT ao governo estadual após pressão de pré-campanha de Lula
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) directory in Rio Grande do Sul decided to support the PDT's pre-candidate for state governor, Juliana Brizola, after pressure from national party leaders. The decision was made in the context of the 2026 election pre-campaign, reflecting coordination among parties allied to the federal government. The move aims to strengthen a progressive front in the state.

item.title: Em resolução, Novo exige que candidatos ao Senado apoiem impeachment de ministros do STF
item.description: The Novo Party has required its Senate candidates for the 2026 election to pledge support for the impeachment of STF ministers in cases of responsibility crime, abuse of authority, or breach of decorum, per a resolution published in the Official Gazette. The party also banned coalitions with the Brazil of Hope Federation (PT, PCdoB, PV) and the PSOL-Rede Federation due to ideological incompatibility, and established candidate selection criteria based on party alignment, moral integrity, and electoral viability.

item.title: Nos bastidores da politica, Gabs se destaca ao impulsionar posicionamento digital de liderancas
item.description: Gabs, leader of Gabs Agency, has emerged as a key behind-the-scenes figure in Brazilian politics by enhancing the digital positioning of political leaders and pre-candidates through strategic digital marketing, social media management, and technological tools. Her work spans from building public image to supporting elected officials, adapting messaging to real-time voter behavior on social media. This highlights the growing influence of strategic communication professionals in shaping political success in today’s digital-driven landscape.

item.title: Nikolas diz ter suplicado para Alcolumbre pautar PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) said he appealed to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP) to schedule analysis of the presidential veto on the Dosimetry Bill, vetoed by Lula on January 8, 2026. The lawmaker stated the request stems from conscience and Christian mercy, seeking relief for affected families. Alcolumbre confirmed he intends to convene a National Congress session as soon as possible to deliberate on the veto.

item.title: Vilão do endividamento, cartão de crédito rotativo cresce; empréstimos beiraram R$ 400 bilhões em 2025
item.description: The use of Brazil's credit card revolving debt reached nearly R$400 billion in 2025, becoming a major driver of population indebtedness. With interest rates at 436% per year and a delinquency rate of 63.5%, the Central Bank warns that many Brazilians treat this emergency credit line as regular income, necessitating structural discussions for healthier credit alternatives.

item.title: Caso Master pode levar Messias antecipadamente ao Senado para ‘pré-sabatina’
item.description: President Lula's nominee to the Supreme Federal Court, Jorge Messias, may be summoned to appear before the Senate's Economic Affairs Committee (CAE) for an informal 'pre-hearing' regarding his role in the Attorney General's Office during the Banco Master case, ahead of his formal confirmation hearing in the Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ). The move, led by Senator Renan Calheiros, aims to anticipate the confirmation debate, with expectations of a more favorable tone given the government's majority in the CAE. Messias has already met with most senators and is seeking to finalize support before returning from vacation.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Com indefinição sobre jornada 6×1 e Master na pauta, governo busca priorizar a economia
item.description: The Lula government plans to send a bill to Congress this week to reduce the workweek from 44 to 40 hours without salary reduction and shift from a 6×1 to a 5×2 schedule, under urgency regime, as part of its electoral agenda. Despite tensions with Chamber President Hugo Motta and remarks about the Master case and STF independence, the administration’s main focus remains the economy, including measures to mitigate Middle East war impacts, new rural credit lines, and actions to curb household indebtedness.

item.title: Galípolo evita jogo político, faz depoimento técnico e vira alvo de críticas do PT e no Planalto
item.description: Central Bank President Gabriel Galípolo delivered a technical testimony before the Organized Crime CPI, refraining from assigning blame to his predecessor Roberto Campos Neto regarding the Banco Master frauds. His stance was criticized by PT members and Planalto aides as an attempt to shield Campos Neto, perceived as politically motivated omissions. Although Galípolo stated Lula instructed him not to protect or pursue anyone, his reliance on internal BC audits disappointed government allies who expected a more critical stance.

item.title: 'Supersecretária' coordenará programa de governo da reeleição de Tarcísio
item.description: Natália Resende, known as the 'supersecretary' of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans), has been appointed to coordinate the government program for his 2026 re-election campaign. The appointment underscores the centralization of the campaign team around key figures from the current state administration.

item.title: Indicado por Lula para o STF, Messias estará oficialmente de férias até o fim do mês
item.description: Attorney General of the Union Jorge Messias, nominated by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for a seat on the Supreme Federal Court (STF), officially began his vacation on Wednesday, April 8. The leave will last until April 30, as published in the Official Gazette of the Union on Thursday, April 9. The vacation was authorized by a dispatch signed by President Lula himself.

item.title: Lula ataca bets de olho no voto de mulheres cansadas das dívidas dos homens
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized online betting platforms (bets) in an interview with ICL Notícias, emphasizing how men's gambling habits increase family debt and burden women's household budgets. He aims to leverage this issue to strengthen support among women voters, a key demographic that backed him in 2022, ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Lula pede que eleitores comparem governos, e teste no Google mostra respostas favoráveis com base em PT e MST
item.description: Lula urges voters to use Google to compare government performance, highlighting investments in literacy and education, with AI-generated responses favoring his administration based on petista and government sources. GLOBO’s tests confirmed that Google’s AI summaries tend to be positive toward the government due to reliance on PT, Instituto Lula, MST, and CanalGov. According to the latest Quaest poll, Flávio Bolsonaro is gaining among independent voters, narrowing Lula’s lead, with both candidates tied at 41% in a potential runoff.

item.title: Filme sobre Bolsonaro com ator de 'A Paixão de Cristo' ganha data de estreia e pôster
item.description: Directed by Cyrus Nowrasteh and starring Jim Caviezel, 'Dark Horse' portrays the political journey of Jair Bolsonaro, from his time as a congressman to the 2018 assassination attempt, and is set to premiere in Brazilian theaters on September 11, 2024, just weeks before the first round of the elections. Filmed in both Brazil and the United States, the movie features international actors such as Lynn Collins and Esai Morales, alongside Brazilian actor Felipe Folgosi, and includes appearances by Bolsonaro’s sons, Flávio and Carlos, during filming in São Paulo.

item.title: Ala do STF vê Lula em modo campanha ao se afastar do caso Master
item.description: STF ministers, including Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes, claim Lula has entered campaign mode by publicly distancing himself from the Supreme Court to avoid electoral wear, amid perceptions of government-Court entanglement. Lula advised Moraes not to let the Master case damage his reputation, highlighting his legacy from the January 8 ruling and suggesting recusal in cases involving his wife. While government allies see the move as strategic, STF ministers express irritation, warning it could create unnecessary tensions between the Branches of government.

item.title: Por sprint final na busca de votos no Senado, Messias tira férias da AGU
item.description: The Attorney General, Jorge Messias, took time off to focus on lobbying senators for his Supreme Court nomination. He has already met with nearly all senators, and allies say the outlook improves daily. The rapporteur, Weverton Rocha, has announced he will vote in favor, citing Messias’ renowned legal expertise.

item.title: Deputada ameaça usar lei Maria da Penha contra Erika Hilton
item.description: Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP), president of the Women's Rights Defense Committee in the Chamber of Deputies, faced a motion of repudiation from opposition female lawmakers during a committee meeting on Wednesday, the 8th. Opponents challenged her leadership and threatened to invoke the Maria da Penha Law against her. The incident highlights political and ideological tensions within Brazil's congressional efforts to advance women's rights.

item.title: Alcolumbre convocará sessão para votar veto ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre announced he will convene a joint session of Congress to review President Lula’s full veto of the Dosimetria Bill, which seeks to reduce sentences for those involved in the January 8 events. Alcolumbre said he is coordinating with Chamber President Hugo Motta and will exercise his constitutional authority to set the agenda. Critics call the bill a total amnesty, while supporters argue it only establishes proportionality in sentencing.

item.title: Levantamento analisa 56 milhões de postagens nas redes e mapeia crise reputacional no STF
item.description: A study by Ativaweb DataLab analyzed 56.2 million public social media mentions in March 2026, revealing that 78.6% of mentions of the STF were negative, indicating a structural reputational crisis. The association between individual ministers’ rulings, personal conduct, and public perceptions of authoritarianism or corruption is transferring personal criticism to the institution as a whole, with Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Nunes Marques cited most negatively, while André Mendonça stands out positively.

item.title: Nunes Marques vai criar força-tarefa no TSE para segurança das eleições
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques, set to assume the TSE presidency in May, plans a task force with regional electoral courts to review over 500,000 electronic voting machines ahead of the October presidential elections. He also aims to coordinate with states on data transmission, establish cybersecurity partnerships with institutions and universities, and increase indigenous participation through training and information dissemination.

item.title: O desafio de Lula é ser candidato sem deixar de ser estadista
item.description: The article discusses the challenge faced by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in balancing his candidacy for re-election in 2026 with the maintenance of a statesmanlike posture, avoiding purely partisan discourse. Journalist Maria Inês Nassif emphasizes that Lula must govern with broad support and a national vision, despite electoral pressures and political polarization. The balance between party leadership and institutional responsibility is presented as central to his legitimacy and effectiveness in a potential second term.

item.title: Messias tem menos de 30 votos garantidos em sua busca por apoio no Senado
item.description: According to Davi Alcolumbre, Lula’s nominee to the STF, Jorge Messias, would have between 22 and 25 guaranteed votes in the Senate, below the 41 needed for approval. This signals strong parliamentary resistance to his nomination. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Base de Lula redige 'PEC da Integridade' para Tręs Poderes, mas foco no STF
item.description: Allies of President Lula in the Senate have begun drafting a PEC to establish the 'Public Integrity Statute', imposing rules and restrictions on authorities across the Three Powers, with a primary focus on the Judiciary, especially the STF. The proposal aims to enforce stricter ethical standards for high-ranking public officials, including Supreme Court justices.

item.title: Sem votos, suplentes tiveram R$ 1,7 bi em emendas no Senado | Podcast UOL Prime #117
item.description: Over the past eight years, 51 alternates have assumed Senate seats without receiving direct votes, allocating R$1.7 billion in parliamentary amendments — an amount exceeding what many elected senators distribute. These substitutes, often businesspeople with limited political experience, tend to vote more frequently with the government and, in some cases, use their mandate to benefit their own businesses, as seen with Margareth Buzetti (MT) and Giordano (Podemos-SP).

item.title: Relator aposta em PEC 6x1 e minimiza projeto prometido por Lula
item.description: The rapporteur of PEC 6×1 in the Chamber’s CCJ, Paulo Azi (União-BA), said he trusts his proposal will advance in Congress despite Lula’s promise to send a bill on the matter. He views the president’s statement as more of an electoral move for 2026 than an effective legislative action, arguing only a constitutional amendment would withstand judicial review at the Supreme Court. Azi also stressed that removing Congress’s leadership on this issue would be inconsistent, given Lula did not prioritize it in previous terms.

item.title: PL avalia mais uma mulher para vice de Flávio Bolsonaro; saiba quem
item.description: The PL is evaluating federal deputy Clarissa Tércio (PP-PE) as a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro, after Senator Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) declined the offer. Clarissa, 41, confirmed she was approached and said she would accept the invitation if it adds value to the ticket, emphasizing her support for former President Jair Bolsonaro and her Northeastern background. However, negotiations are more advanced with deputy Simone Marchetto (PP-SP), linked to Catholic religious leadership.

item.title: 'A criminalidade está misturada no Brasil. Temos o Estado oficial e o Estado paralelo', diz coordenador de campanha de Lula
item.description: Wellington Dias, minister and political coordinator of Lula's campaign, acknowledged that security is a sensitive issue ahead of the 2026 elections and downplayed the growth of Flávio Bolsonaro in polls, stating that crime in Brazil involves both the official state and a 'parallel state'.

item.title: É #FAKE que Brasil perdeu vaga em comissão de direitos humanos da OEA e foi classificado como 'país governado por ditador'
item.description: It is false that Brazil lost its seat in the OEA’s Inter-American Commission on Human Rights for being labeled a 'dictatorship-led country'. Brazil voluntarily withdrew its candidacy following a diplomatic agreement with Mexico, and the OEA denied issuing any such classification. The misleading content, featuring AI-generated imagery, has circulated since July 2025.

item.title: Pesquisa expõe ‘racha’ entre homens e mulheres no apoio a Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll reveals a significant gender split in support for Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of the 2026 elections, highlighting polarization beyond the traditional petista-bolsonarist divide. Data suggests that voting differences between male and female electorates will deepen, reinforcing trends seen in 2018 and 2022. Full access to the article requires a subscription.

item.title: Estadão e Record firmam parceria para debates presidenciais e ao governo de São Paulo
item.description: Estadão and Record have partnered to host presidential and São Paulo gubernatorial debates in the 2026 elections. The presidential debate is scheduled for September 27 (first round) and, if needed, October 18 (second round), both at 9 PM. The São Paulo gubernatorial debate will take place on September 21 at 1:25 PM, with a potential second round on October 13 at 1:20 PM. The partnership aims to expand access to high-quality debates amid an expected polarization between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ).

item.title: O Rio em julgamento
item.description: The STF's judgment on whether the election to replace former Rio de Janeiro Governor Cláudio Castro — who resigned to avoid an almost certain impeachment — will be indirect or direct is triggering a realignment of forces within the Court, with potential consequences for upcoming cases like the Banco Master matter. Castro stepped down to evade a near-certain removal, and the outcome of this decision may affect the political and juridical balance in the tribunal.

item.title: Por que não é possível se candidatar sem partido no Brasil
item.description: Brazil's 1988 Constitution mandates party affiliation as a mandatory requirement for running for elective office, reinforcing pluripartisanship as the foundation of post-dictatorship democracy. This rule was upheld by the Supreme Court and the Elections Law (9.597/97), which prohibit independent candidacies, as parties are responsible for organizing candidacies, structuring campaigns, and ensuring governability. Experts state that Brazil's electoral system is structured around parties, making independent candidacies incompatible with the institutional design.

item.title: Fala de Lula sobre Moraes mostra que roteiro para se descolar do caso Master precisa de ajuste
item.description: Lula acknowledged that trying to hide or downplay the Master case is no longer viable, as the Supreme Court's image is tarnished and the scandal could spill over to his government. In an interview with ICL, he said the Court must provide a convincing explanation to society and that justices cannot become millionaires improperly. The president signaled that the strategy of silence needs to be revised amid growing public pressure.

item.title: Em mensagens, presidenciável do MBL relatava uso de cogumelos mágicos
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pre-candidate from the MBL, privately admitted in messages from the Cannipapo Instagram group to using magic mushrooms (Psilocybe cubensis), describing psychedelic experiences and confirming consumption. Despite publicly campaigning against drug trafficking, he acknowledged using the substance at least twice between November 2024 and October 2025, as verified by Metrópoles and confirmed by Santos himself.

item.title: Regra que pode 'unificar' eleições no Rio nunca foi aplicada pela Justiça Eleitoral para governadores
item.description: A 2018 TSE resolution allows supplementary elections to be held on the same date as ordinary ones in exceptional cases, but this rule has never been applied for governors. During the STF trial on Rio’s supplementary gubernatorial election, ministers suggested using this rule to unify elections in October, though experts note no precedent exists at the state level. Minister Fux voted for an indirect election, limited to state deputies of Alerj.

item.title: A eleição que pode acabar no primeiro turno
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election could be decided in the first round, as it was in 1998, the last time this occurred. Analysts consider this possibility real, despite the absence of 'sudden death' rules in electoral processes. The content is an exclusive article for subscribers, encouraging access through registration at the publication's link.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro amplia opções de vice no PP e eleva pressão sobre Tereza Cristina
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has expanded his options for vice president in his pre-campaign, testing PP names to pressure Tereza Cristina into accepting the ticket. The vice-presidential pick hinges on a broader agreement between PP and União Brasil, which faces internal resistance due to the PL’s gains during the party window. If the federation fails, Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema emerges as a backup option for the bolsonarist ticket.

item.title: 'A Rede não tem dono' x 'retomar valores': entenda o embate entre Marina e a cúpula do partido, ligada a Heloísa Helena
item.description: The internal conflict in Rede Sustentability intensified between the national leadership, led by Paulo Lamac and allied with Heloísa Helena, and Marina Silva’s faction after she announced she would remain in the party to 'recover core values'. The party leadership claims democratic election and rejects accusations of authoritarianism, stating the party has no owner and must respect collective decisions. Marina, despite internal rifts and offers from the PT and PSB, reiterated her commitment to the party she helped found, keeping alive her potential Senate candidacy on Haddad’s ticket.

item.title: Lula teve encontro com Alcolumbre três dias antes de mandar mensagem de indicação de Messias ao Senado
item.description: Three days before sending the presidential message nominating Jorge Messias to the STF, Lula met with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre at the Alvorada Palace, accompanied by Rodrigo Pacheco. Although Alcolumbre did not guarantee approval, Lula felt the resistance to Messias had eased, with Pacheco also discussing his Minas gubernatorial bid with Lula’s backing.

item.title: De ex-ministros de Lula a auxiliares de Bolsonaro: os nomes na lista de pagamentos do Master, que soma R$ 66 milhões
item.description: The Master Bank reported to the Federal Revenue at least R$65.83 million in payments to party officials, former ministers, and a former president between 2023 and 2025, according to documents obtained by O GLOBO. The recipients include figures linked to both Lula’s government and Bolsonaro’s allies. Bank owner Daniel Vorcaro is detained on suspicion of fraud, while beneficiaries deny wrongdoing and claim legitimate relations with the institution.

item.title: Como fica o mapa dos governos estaduais com as trocas e renúncias para eleição 2026
item.description: Following the end of the incompatibility window, 10 states and the Federal District have new governors, reshaping the map of support for the 2026 presidential pre-candidates. Lula (PT) lost backing in Espírito Santo but retains support in 11 states, while Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) gained support in Acre and sees Amazonas and Rio de Janeiro under interim leadership. The PSD expanded its governorships to six, becoming the party with the strongest state presence.

item.title: MG decide de novo? Estado mais disputado segue indefinido para eleição
item.description: Minas Gerais, Brazil's second-largest electoral college, remains undecided for the 2026 elections, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro vying for support in a highly polarized scenario. In 2022, the state recorded the tightest result in the country, with Lula winning by just 50.2% to 49.8%, a margin of fewer than 50,000 votes. Despite efforts from both sides, neither has secured a solid electoral base in Minas, while the PL has yet to decide whether to run its own candidate or ally with figures like Cleitinho or Mateus Simões.

item.title: Brasil se encamina a unas elecciones sin mujeres candidatas a la presidencia por primera vez en más de 20 años
item.description: Brazil may hold its 2026 presidential election without any female candidates for the first time since 2002. The race is shaping up to be between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, seeking re-election, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving house arrest. Other pre-candidates, such as Ronaldo Caiado, are also men from right-wing parties, highlighting the lack of female representation in the presidential race.
